links.comparator_used: LLM output shown without uncertainty information (baseline condition), and across different uncertainty granularities (output-level, relation-level, token-level)
links.outcome: User agreement with the AI, user confidence in own answers, and external verification behavior (internet searches, checking URLs)
links.effect: Token-level uncertainty increased agreement with the AI; output- and relation-level uncertainty did not increase agreement but reduced users' confidence in their own answers; relation-level uncertainty also reduced external verification.
links.tradeoff: Relation-level uncertainty steered users away from independent fact-checking toward reliance on the LLM and its uncertainty cues; token-level uncertainty increased agreement with the AI (risk of over-reliance).
links.quote: Token-level uncertainty increased users' agreement with the AI, whereas output- and relation-level uncertainty did not increase agreement but instead reduced users' confidence in their own answers.

links.comparator_used: Alternative uncertainty display formats for the same LLM output (output-level vs relation-level vs token-level)
links.outcome: User agreement, self-confidence, and external verification when answering medical questions
links.effect: Distinct behavioral effects by granularity: token-level raised agreement with the AI; output- and relation-level lowered user confidence; relation-level reduced external verification.
links.tradeoff: Relation-level display reduced independent fact-checking; token-level display increased agreement with the AI.
links.quote: Our findings reveal distinct behavioral effects as a function of uncertainty granularity.

design_hint: uncertainty display at different granularities (output, relation, token level)
